name: io.github.2016judea/substack-in-print
title: Substack in Print
description: Turn your Substack into a printed magazine, with a public-domain artist in residence for the plates

tools.name: read_substack_archive
tools.description: Lists a Substack publication's posts, newest first, up to 100 per call: slug, title, subtitle, date, word count, whether it is paywalled (paid posts print only their free preview), and Substack's one-line description. Accepts a handle (aidanjude), a subdomain (aidanjude.substack.com) or a custom domain. Returns next_cursor when there are more posts; passing it back returns the next 100. Example calls: {"substack":"aidanjude"}; {"substack":"www.example.com","cursor":"c:eyJ..."}.

substack.description: Substack handle, subdomain or custom domain

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous call, to read further back

tools.name: read_substack_post
tools.description: Returns one post's title, subtitle, date, word count, image count and full text as plain paragraphs (up to 20,000 characters; truncated is true past that). Paid posts return only the free preview Substack shares publicly. Example: {"substack":"aidanjude","slug":"nov-26-pt4"}.

substack.description: Substack handle, subdomain or custom domain

tools.name: find_artist_works
tools.description: Searches the Art Institute of Chicago and the Cleveland Museum of Art open-access collections for works by one artist that the museum itself flags public domain / CC0, and drops everything else. Each work comes back with its museum id (aic:NNN or cma:NNN), title, date, medium, whether it is a line work (print or drawing, which also suits a white-on-black stencil), orientation, pixel size, the resolution it reaches as a full-bleed page (full_page_bleed_ppi; 200+ prints sharp), a thumbnail, the museum page and the credit line. The summary counts how many works print a full page sharp, which says whether the artist can fill an issue (about 8 to 12 distinct works for a 24 to 40 page issue). Living or recently dead artists usually return nothing: their work is not public domain. Example: {"artist":"Albrecht Dürer"}; {"artist":"Hokusai","limit":20}.

tools.name: lay_out_issue
tools.description: Saves an issue (the essays in order, the title, the artist in residence and the works for its plates) and returns a short link to a page where it is already laid out as a stapled 8.5 x 11 in print magazine: cover art, contents, each essay set in print type, a frontispiece, full-page plates on spare pages and white-on-black stencils where an essay ends early, with 'Artist in residence: <name>' on the back cover. The page pages through like the printed copy and takes the order (quantity, then Stripe checkout); copies are printed and shipped to one address, or mailed to a list of the writer's readers. Every work is re-checked against the museum's public-domain flag; anything not flagged, or not by the named artist, is dropped. work_ids are optional: without them, or when too few are given for the plate slots, the artist's sharpest public-domain works fill the rest. Returns the link, the estimated page count, the essays it found, the works on hand and example prices. Example: {"substack":"aidanjude","post_slugs":["oct-26-pt1","oct-26-pt2"],"artist":"Albrecht Dürer","title":"Periodicals","work_ids":["aic:51498","aic:55330"]}.

substack.description: Substack handle, subdomain or custom domain

post_slugs.description: The essays, in reading order, by slug

artist.description: The artist in residence the writer picked

title.description: The magazine's name on the cover (default: the publication's name)

work_ids.description: Optional: works from find_artist_works in order of preference (aic:NNN / cma:NNN); the first portrait one that prints full page sharp is the cover unless cover_work_id is given

cover_work_id.description: Optional: the work for the front cover

tools.name: price_print_run
tools.description: Prices a print run of a stapled 8.5 x 11 in magazine on 100 lb satin paper: Mixam's print price for that page count and quantity (quoted from Mixam's own calculator, date included), ground shipping to one US address, sales tax, our margin, card fees, the total and the price per copy. With mail_to_readers it adds, per reader, First-Class Mail postage for a flat at the issue's weight, an envelope and handling (copies come to us and we mail each one). Example: {"pages":28,"copies":10}; {"pages":24,"copies":40,"mail_to_readers":true}.

pages.description: Page count including covers, a multiple of 4 (lay_out_issue gives an estimate; the issue page shows the exact count)

mail_to_readers.description: true = we mail one copy to each reader on a list the writer uploads (copies = number of readers)

tools.name: print_edition_estimate
tools.description: Returns a publication's name, which of its public posts suit a stapled magazine (titled, 600 to 5,000 words), an estimated page count, and the price of one printed copy and of ten. It does not lay out, print or charge for an issue.

substack.description: The Substack: a URL, a subdomain or a custom domain

essays.description: How many essays to estimate for (default 8)

tools.name: best_substack_posts_for_print
tools.description: A Substack's posts sorted for print: public, titled newsletter posts between 600 and 5,000 words first, longest first, each with its word count and an estimated page count, and the posts set aside (paid, very short, podcasts, threads) with the reason. Example questions: which of my posts should go in the magazine; my best essays for print; what would make a good print issue from my archive.

substack.description: The Substack: a URL, a subdomain or a custom domain

tools.name: cost_to_print_my_substack
tools.description: What a printed issue of a Substack costs: pages estimated from the chosen posts' word and image counts (or the given page count), then the itemised price (Mixam printing, shipping, tax, Stripe, our margin) at 1, 5, 10 and 25 copies or the number asked. Example questions: how much to print my Substack; cost of 20 copies of my newsletter as a magazine; price of a 40-page zine.

substack.description: The Substack: a URL, a subdomain or a custom domain

post_slugs.description: The essays, by slug; without them the most recent print-suited posts are used

essays.description: How many recent essays when no slugs are given (default 8)

pages.description: A page count, instead of a Substack

tools.name: how_many_pages_will_my_magazine_be
tools.description: The estimated page count of a printed issue: cover, contents, frontispiece, each essay from its words and images, and a back page, rounded up to a multiple of 4, and whether it fits a stapled magazine (80 pages). The issue page gives the exact count once laid out. Example questions: how many pages would my essays make; will 12 posts fit in one issue; how long would the magazine be.

substack.description: The Substack: a URL, a subdomain or a custom domain

tools.name: price_to_mail_printed_copies
tools.description: Returns the itemised price of printing one copy per reader and mailing each copy by US First-Class: printing, shipping the batch, envelopes, postage and handling. It does not send mail and it does not charge anyone. Reader count is 1 to 100; pass a page count or a Substack to estimate one.

readers.description: How many readers get a copy (1 to 100; the price grid on file stops at 100 copies)

substack.description: The Substack: a URL, a subdomain or a custom domain

tools.name: is_this_artist_public_domain
tools.description: Whether an artist's works are public domain and on hand to print, from the Art Institute of Chicago and Cleveland Museum of Art open-access collections: works found, how many print a full page sharp, line works, life dates, and whether there are enough for an issue (8 full-page works), with three sample works and their credit lines. Example questions: can I use Hokusai in my magazine; is Aubrey Beardsley public domain; does Gustave Doré have enough prints for an issue.
